agree.reason: The 20-mile chain gap and the offer to share invoices and meet before May 1 give a skeptical director something concrete to check, though the letter puts no dollar total on the loss, so it still reads somewhat like a routine rate complaint.

honest.reason: It correctly drops the 'third will close' claim and hedges the nine closures, but 'losing money every time we do' and 'that loss on one prescription in five' stretch an average shortfall on 20 generics to all plan prescriptions and ignore that some of the loss is made up on brand-name drugs.

works_the_facts.reason: It derives no figures from the brief: it never uses the 3,100 prescriptions Reilly Drug filled, never gives a yearly loss for one pharmacy or for the 38, and never turns the $1.80 into a total the reader could weigh.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the status quo as the facts show it: two pharmacies ready to stop filling for plan members, nine closures in two years, and a drive of more than 20 miles or a mail-order wait in 14 counties, though it doesn't spell out the trend.

qualification.reason: The hedge on the closures is fair and the May 1 and July 1 dates are checkable, but no condition carries a number and a consequence the reader could verify, such as how many members would lose their nearest pharmacy.

objections.reason: It meets the 'plenty of chains' belief with the 14 counties and the 20-mile gap, and the invoice offer answers 'you complain every year', but it leaves the obvious brand-drug offset objection unaddressed.

fit.reason: It is a one-page open letter, signed and addressed correctly, and works both for the plan and for newspaper readers.
